rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw' backward beat references in this file; it is the training's first artefact, so there is nothing prior to point at.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo beat in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "What to bring": line 20: "**Four sizes off your backlog. Not four slices of one task.**" — a full two-sentence closing line bolded whole, not a ≲5-word handle (named law/checklist-item/coined term). Harm: this is exactly the shape rule 9 exists to stop — a bolded mechanism/narrative sentence competing with the four genuine bullet handles above it (Trivial bug, A small multi-file task, A small feature, A bigger piece) for the reader's eye, diluting which bold actually marks something to remember.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the bold, or shorten to a short handle like a caption under the list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No wrapper/inclusion change touched in this file; nothing suggests content dropped from the composed deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
